items.title: The header is only a fallback
items.body:
`CurrentUser` starts with `context.Request.Cookies.TryGetValue("globalhire_user_id", out var id)`. Only when that fails does it read the `Authorization` header. Here the cookie holds "user-client", so the header is never read and the caller is Casey Client.

- *Header always wins*: the code reads the header only inside the "no cookie" branch.
- *Conflict means 401*: the function never compares the two sources.
- *Most privileged wins*: roles are not consulted when resolving the id.

items.title: The only date rule is end after start
items.body:
`POST /api/leave-requests` resolves the worker, checks `CanAccessWorker`, and rejects only `input.EndDate < input.StartDate`. Nothing checks the length, a balance or the country's statutory vacation days, so a three-year request is stored as given (finding A6).

- *One calendar year*: no such limit exists in the handler.
- *Longer than vacation days*: country rules are not consulted here.
- *Trimmed end date*: the dates are stored exactly as sent.

excerpts.quote: if (input.EndDate < input.StartDate) return Error("endDate must be on or after startDate");

items.title: "Can see" used as "can approve"
items.body:
`ReviewLeave` authorises with `CanAccessWorker(actor, worker)`. Its second clause is `actor.Role == Role.WORKER && actor.WorkerId == worker.Id`, which is true for Maya on her own request. Nothing else is checked, so she approves her own leave and is recorded as reviewer (finding A4).

- *Workers cannot review*: that is the TypeScript original's `canReviewPeopleWorkflows`, not this code.
- *Separation of duties*: no rule compares reviewer and requester.
- *Flag for a manager*: there is no second-approval step.

items.title: Working one payroll item by hand
items.body:
Overtime counts only APPROVED timesheets whose week starts inside the period, so 8 hours, not 14. Hourly rate is `SalaryAmount / 160m` = 30; overtime pay is 8 * 30 * 1.5 = 360; gross is 5,160. Net is `grossPay - employeeTax`, with employee tax 20% = 1,032, so 4,128. Employer cost (14%) is a separate line, never subtracted from net.

- *4,800 and 3,840* drops the approved overtime.
- *5,430 and 4,344* also counts the SUBMITTED timesheet's 6 hours.
- *Net 4,437.60* subtracts the employer cost instead of the employee tax.

items.title: Three gates before ACTIVE
items.body:
`Activate` checks, in order: status is ONBOARDING; no required onboarding task is anything but APPROVED; the employment `ContractStatus` is SIGNED. The first two pass here, and SENT fails the third with "Employment contract must be SIGNED before activation".

- *Activated because the tasks are done*: the contract gate still applies.
- *CLIENT_ADMIN only*: the route allows EOR_SPECIALIST as well.
- *Activated with a flag*: Activate returns an error and leaves the status unchanged.

excerpts.quote: if (employment?.ContractStatus != ContractStatus.SIGNED) return (null, "Employment contract must be SIGNED before activation");

items.title: Start here: GlobalHire Lite and its two implementations
items.body:
GlobalHire Lite is an employer-of-record demo: hire international workers, onboard them, approve leave and timesheets, run payroll, offboard. The repo holds two versions of it. The TypeScript original under `globalhire-lite/apps/` is entirely commented out; the live code is the C# ASP.NET Core rewrite under `globalhire-lite/migrated-dotnet/`, with an in-memory store.

The `fable/` folder is the guide. Read in this order:

1. `fable/README.md` and `fable/01-codebase-overview.md`: the domain, both stacks, and a side-by-side table.
2. `fable/02-what-is-done-well.md`: the payroll state machine, tenant scoping and the business-rule tests.
3. `fable/03-what-needs-improvement.md`: the defects, security first.

This pack tests the **live** .NET code. Keep `Program.cs`, `Services/WorkerService.cs` and `Services/PayrollService.cs` open, since most handlers are minimal-API lambdas in `Program.cs`.

excerpts.quote: This folder is a structured code review of the `globalhire-lite` codebase

items.title: Identity, roles and per-record access in Program.cs
items.body:
Three helpers at the bottom of `Program.cs` decide who is calling and what they may touch:

- `CurrentUser` turns a request into a user. Read the order in which it consults the cookie and the `Authorization` header, and what it does with the value it finds.
- `CanAccessWorker` and `CanAccessOrganization` answer "may this actor touch this worker or org". List the three clauses of `CanAccessWorker` and which roles each one lets through.
- Login at the top of the file: compare how it checks the password with how `User` is defined in `Domain/Entities.cs`.

Then go handler by handler for the mutations (onboarding submit, approve and reject; leave and timesheet review; offboarding; worker PATCH and activate). For each, write down which of these checks it calls: a role check, an ownership check, a status check. `fable/03` sections A3 to A5 discuss the gaps; confirm each against the lines.

items.title: An error state nothing resets
items.body:
`reload()` increments `tick`, which is in the effect's dependency list, so the loader runs again and `.then(setData)` stores the new data. The effect never calls `setError("")`, so the message from the first failure stays in state and the page keeps showing it (finding B3, problem 3).

- *Error cleared*: no code path clears it.
- *Stays failed until remount*: the retry does fetch and set data.
- *tick does not re-run the effect*: tick is the first dependency of the effect.

items.title: Any status, straight from the URL
items.body:
`PATCH /api/offboarding-cases/{id}/{status}` binds any `OffboardingStatus` value from the route, checks only `CanAccessWorker`, assigns it, and sets the worker to TERMINATED whenever the new status is COMPLETED. A REQUESTED case therefore completes at once and the worker is terminated.

- *Cannot jump*: there are no transition rules in this handler.
- *Worker stays OFFBOARDING*: the COMPLETED branch terminates the worker.
- *EOR specialist only*: a same-org CLIENT_ADMIN passes CanAccessWorker.

items.title: A credential with a default value
items.body:
`User.Password` is declared with the initialiser `"password123"`, and the seed never sets it, so both seeded users have that password. Login compares `candidate.Password == input.Password` in plaintext (finding A2).

- *Password123!* is the README's credential for the commented-out TypeScript seed, which does not run.
- *Reset first*: there is no reset flow; the default simply applies.
- *Random at startup*: nothing generates or prints passwords.

items.title: Currency is part of the duplicate key
items.body:
`Create` refuses a run only when one already exists with the same organization, period start, period end **and** currency. A CAD run for the USD run's dates matches on the first three but not the fourth, so a new DRAFT run is created.

- *Already exists for that period*: that error needs the currency to match too.
- *Idempotent return*: that is the invoice endpoint's behaviour, not payroll Create.
- *Currency must match the org*: Create never compares the run currency with anything about the organization.

items.title: A role check is not an ownership check
items.body:
The approve handler checks that there is an actor and that the actor is not a WORKER, then finds the task by id and sets it APPROVED with `ReviewedById = actor.Id`. It never looks up the task's worker or compares organizations, and it does not check the task's current status (finding A3).

- *403 for another org*: no organization comparison exists in this handler.
- *404*: the task lookup is by id across all organizations.
- *Must be SUBMITTED*: there is no status check before the update.

excerpts.quote: if (actor.Role is Role.WORKER) return Error("Forbidden", StatusCodes.Status403Forbidden);

items.title: The generic PATCH outranks the guarded transition
items.body:
The PATCH route allows CLIENT_ADMIN, EOR_SPECIALIST and PLATFORM_ADMIN, then calls `WorkerService.Update`, which runs `if (input.Status is not null) worker.Status = input.Status.Value;`. The task and contract checks live only in `Activate`, so PATCH sets ACTIVE directly (finding A5, mass assignment).

- *Tasks must be approved* and *contract must be SIGNED* are Activate's errors; Update never runs them.
- *Only via /activate*: nothing restricts which fields Update accepts.

excerpts.quote: if (input.Status is not null) worker.Status = input.Status.Value;

items.title: Payroll maths and the guarded workflows
items.body:
`Services/PayrollService.cs` is the best-guarded code here: Create, Calculate, Approve and Lock each check the run's status before acting. Read Create's duplicate check and list every field it compares.

For Calculate, work through one worker by hand: which workers are included, which timesheets count toward overtime (status and date window), how the hourly rate is derived from the salary, the overtime multiplier, and which of the two country-rule percentages is subtracted to get net pay. Note where rounding happens.

`WorkerService.Activate` is the other guarded transition. List its three conditions. Then compare it with `WorkerService.Update` and ask which fields Update will write when they are present in the request.

For the frontend, `useLoad` in `migrated-dotnet/src/GlobalHireLite.Web/src/App.tsx` is a hand-rolled data hook. Read which state setters the effect calls, and on which outcome.

excerpts.quote: public sealed class PayrollService(InMemoryGlobalHireStore store, AuthorizationService authorization)
Workflow state machines with guarded transitions

items.title: Presenting an id is the whole login
items.body:
With no cookie, `CurrentUser` takes the text after "Bearer " and returns `store.Users.FirstOrDefault(user => user.Id == id)`. "user-admin" is the seeded platform admin's id, so the request runs as Ada Admin. Nothing is signed or checked (finding A1).

- *Must be a signed JWT*: that is the TypeScript original; the live code has no signature.
- *Cookie required*: the header is accepted when no cookie is present.
- *Casey Client*: her id is "user-client", not "user-admin".

excerpts.quote: return id is null ? null : store.Users.FirstOrDefault(user => user.Id == id);
